heard: NASA fluted Jupiter just to look at the Sun. Standard rockets couldn't push a probe out of Earth's flat orbit, so Ulysses used Jupiter's gravity to loop over the Sun's poles. It launched in 1990 and hit record-shattering speeds. But the mission found far more than just a view. Interstellar dust was 30 times more abundant than scientists expected. The probe even unexpectedly sailed through three separate comet tails. It revealed solar winds moving twice as fast at the poles. To see the Sun from the top, you have to leave home.
